title: Polynomial extension of an augmented simplicial ring resolution is a trivial Kan fibration
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $E$ be any set, and let $P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const} B$ be an augmented simplicial commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Assume every $P_n\to B$ is surjective and the augmentation $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism, where $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ with differential $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i$ for $n>0$ and zero positive terms [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Form $P_\bullet[E]$ by adjoining polynomial variables indexed by $E$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], with every simplicial operator fixing the variables and acting on coefficients. Then every $P_n[E]\to B[E]$ is surjective, and $s(P_\bullet[E])\to B[E][0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Both maps of underlying simplicial sets $P_\bullet\to\operatorname{const} B$ and $P_\bullet[E]\to\operatorname{const}(B[E])$ are trivial Kan fibrations [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. No finiteness assumption on $E$ or polynomiality assumption on the individual $P_n$ is required.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), last paragraph; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution); simplicial.tex Tag 08P1 (lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups). Polynomial extension expanded via finite-support monomial coefficients.

proof.text: Put $I=\{\alpha:E\to\mathbf Z_{\geq0}:\alpha\text{ has finite support}\}$. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], each element of $R[E]$ is uniquely a finite sum $\sum_{\alpha\in I}r_\alpha x^\alpha$. Every simplicial operator $\theta$ of $P_\bullet[E]$ acts by $\sum r_\alpha x^\alpha\mapsto\sum\theta(r_\alpha)x^\alpha$: this is the algebra map prescribed by its coefficient action and its values on variables. Composition and the augmentation identities follow coefficientwise from those for $P_\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Thus the alternating differential is $d(\sum r_\alpha x^\alpha)=\sum d(r_\alpha)x^\alpha$ in every negative cochain degree, and the augmentation in degree zero acts on coefficients. For $b=\sum_{\alpha\in S}b_\alpha x^\alpha\in B[E]$, with $S$ finite, choose $p_\alpha\in P_n$ mapping to $b_\alpha$. Then $\sum_{\alpha\in S}p_\alpha x^\alpha$ maps to $b$, proving surjectivity for each $n$, including $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), last paragraph; finite-support monomial coefficient expansion.

proof.text: For $r=-n<0$, let $z=\sum_{\alpha\in S}z_\alpha x^\alpha$ be a cycle in $s(P_\bullet[E])^r$, with $S$ finite. Step 1 and uniqueness of coefficients give $d(z_\alpha)=0$ for every $\alpha$. The assumed quasi-isomorphism $s(P_\bullet)\to B[0]$ gives $H^r(s(P_\bullet))=0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence for each $\alpha\in S$ choose $w_\alpha\in P_{n+1}$ with $d(w_\alpha)=z_\alpha$. Step 1 gives $d(\sum_{\alpha\in S}w_\alpha x^\alpha)=z$. Thus every negative-degree cycle is a boundary. The argument uses only the finitely many coefficients of this particular $z$ and makes no finiteness assumption on $E$. Positive-degree cohomology vanishes because all positive terms are zero.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), last paragraph; finite-support monomial coefficient expansion.

proof.text: In degree zero every element of $P_0[E]$ is a cycle. The degree-zero augmentation onto $B[E]$ is surjective by Step 1, so its induced map on $H^0$ is surjective. If $z=\sum_{\alpha\in S}z_\alpha x^\alpha\in P_0[E]$ maps to zero, uniqueness of coefficients says that each $z_\alpha$ maps to zero in $B$. The hypothesis that $H^0(s(P_\bullet))\to B$ is an isomorphism says precisely that $\ker(P_0\to B)=\operatorname{im}(d:P_1\to P_0)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Choose $w_\alpha\in P_1$ with $d(w_\alpha)=z_\alpha$ for each $\alpha\in S$; their polynomial sum has differential $z$ by Step 1. Thus the induced $H^0$ map is injective as well. Steps 2 and 3 prove that $s(P_\bullet[E])\to B[E][0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08QV (lemma-polynomial-on-top), last paragraph; finite-support monomial coefficient expansion.

proof.text: Apply the general augmentation criterion in [lem-trf-polynomial-augmentation-boundary], namely its assertion for an arbitrary augmented simplicial $A$-algebra $Q_\bullet$ with degreewise surjective augmentation and a quasi-isomorphism $s(Q_\bullet)\to B[0]$. First use $Q_\bullet=P_\bullet$ with target $B$, for which both hypotheses are assumptions. Next use $Q_\bullet=P_\bullet[E]$ with target $B[E]$; the same base ring $A$ acts through the coefficients. Step 1 verifies the augmented simplicial algebra structure and degreewise surjectivity; Steps 2 and 3 verify the quasi-isomorphism with exactly the nonpositive indexing in that criterion. Its conclusion gives both trivial Kan fibrations, including vertex lifting. The criterion assumes no polynomiality of the terms, and the coefficient arguments used arbitrary finite polynomial supports, so neither polynomiality of $P_n$ nor finiteness of $E$ has been introduced.
